find_entity_by_wikipedia_title.description: Resolve a Wikipedia article title to the Wikidata entity behind it. Use this when you already have an article name and want its structured data. Returns a null entity id when no article matches, rather than failing.
find_entity_by_wikipedia_title.display_name: Find Wikidata entity by Wikipedia title
find_entity_by_wikipedia_title.display_str_template: Find the Wikidata entity for Wikipedia article '{0}'.
find_entity_by_wikipedia_title.name: find_entity_by_wikipedia_title

parameters.description: Wikipedia article title, e.g. Ada Lovelace. Capitalisation and underscores are normalised for you.
parameters.name: title

parameters.description: Which Wikipedia the title belongs to, e.g. enwiki, frwiki, dewiki. Defaults to enwiki.
parameters.name: wikipedia_site

parameters.description: Language code for labels and descriptions, e.g. en, fr, de, ja. Defaults to en.
parameters.name: language

concept_uri.description: Stable RDF identifier. Null when nothing matched.

description.description: One-line description. Null when nothing matched.

entity_id.description: Wikidata entity id for the article, e.g. Q7259. Null when no article matches the title.

label.description: Entity name. Null when nothing matched.

url.description: wikidata.org page for the entity. Null when nothing matched.

get_entity.description: Get everything Wikidata records about one entity: its name, description, aliases, Wikipedia link, and its statements as readable property/value pairs (e.g. 'date of birth' → 1815-12-10). Optionally narrow it to just the properties you need.

aliases: Augusta Ada King, Countess of Lovelace
entity.label: Ada Lovelace

get_entity.name: get_entity

parameters.description: Wikidata entity id, e.g. Q7259. You can get this from the Search Wikidata action.
parameters.name: entity_id

parameters.description: Language code for labels and descriptions, e.g. en, fr, de, ja. Defaults to en.
parameters.name: language

parameters.description: Optional comma-separated property ids to return, e.g. P569,P570,P106. Leave blank to return every statement, which for a well-covered entity can be a few hundred.
parameters.name: properties

parameters.description: Which Wikipedia to link to, e.g. enwiki, frwiki, dewiki. Defaults to enwiki.
parameters.name: wikipedia_site

aliases.description: Other names the entity is known by, e.g. 'Lady Ada'.

label.description: Entity name in the language asked for.

statement_count.description: Number of statements returned, after any property filter.

statements.description: The entity's facts, one entry per property, ordered by property number.

property_id.description: Wikidata property id, e.g. P569 for date of birth.

property_label.description: Readable property name, e.g. 'date of birth'.

values.description: Every value recorded for this property. Wikidata allows more than one, e.g. a person with several occupations. Values the community has marked deprecated are left out.

entity_id.description: Wikidata id this value points at, e.g. Q170790, when the value is another item. Null otherwise. Use it to look the item up with Get Wikidata entity.

unit_id.description: Wikidata id of the unit for a quantity, e.g. Q11573 for metre. Null when the value is not a quantity or has no unit.

value.description: The value as readable text. An item reference is shown as its label (e.g. 'mathematician'), a date as an ISO 8601 timestamp, a quantity as a number. Null when Wikidata records the value as unknown or as known not to exist.

url.description: Human-readable wikidata.org page for the entity.

wikipedia_url.description: Matching Wikipedia article for the chosen site. Null when the entity has no article there.

run_sparql_query.description: Run a SPARQL query against the Wikidata Query Service. Use this for questions no single lookup answers, such as listing every item matching a set of conditions. Returns one row per result with the query's own variable names as keys.
run_sparql_query.display_str_template: Run a SPARQL query against Wikidata.
run_sparql_query.name: run_sparql_query

parameters.description: SPARQL query text. Add a LIMIT clause: the service caps a query at 60 seconds and will reject one that scans too much. Include the wikibase:label service to get readable names alongside ids.
parameters.name: query

rows.description: One entry per result row, keyed by the query's own variable names with the plain values. A variable left unbound for a row, as an OPTIONAL clause can leave it, is absent from that row.

variables.description: The variable names the query selected, in order. These are the keys on each row.

search_entities.description: Search Wikidata for people, places, organisations, works, and concepts by name. Returns the matching entity ids, which the other Wikidata actions take as input.
search_entities.name: search_entities

parameters.description: Text to search for, e.g. Ada Lovelace.
parameters.name: query

parameters.description: Language code for labels and descriptions, e.g. en, fr, de, ja. Defaults to en.
parameters.name: language

parameters.description: How many results to return, 1 to 50. Defaults to 10.
parameters.name: limit

parameters.description: What kind of entity to search for. Defaults to item, which covers people, places, and things. Use property to find the P-ids used in statements.
parameters.name: entity_type

concept_uri.description: Stable RDF identifier, e.g. http://www.wikidata.org/entity/Q7259. This is the form SPARQL queries use.

id.description: Wikidata entity id, e.g. Q7259. Used by the other actions.

label.description: Entity name in the language asked for.

match_text.description: The label or alias that actually matched the search text, which may differ from the entity's main label.

url.description: Human-readable wikidata.org page for the entity.

description: Look up structured facts from Wikidata, the free knowledge base behind Wikipedia: search for entities by name, read an entity's statements as readable property/value pairs, resolve a Wikipedia article to its entity, and run SPARQL queries. No account or API key required.
